title: Slot-pacing mini-bench: latency vs cost (notes)
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental notes from the slot-pacing mini-bench run (May 12–16, 2028). Goal is to compare small-scale slot-based pacing vs opportunistic multiplexing for a conversational microprofile (median tokens 28, taily turns). This is a lightweight capture — not a final report — intended to seed a broader run and inform console heuristics.

Summary (top-level):
- Workloads: synthetic "assist-lite" conversations and a small corpus of recorded sessions (500 sessions).
- Platforms: p3-small-equivalent nodes (8 A100-like vram profile) using runtime build v2.7.2-experimental.
- Knobs: slot-pacing window = {50ms, 100ms, 250ms}, multiplex batch policy = opportunistic until slot fill or 10ms max; KV-cache enabled.
- Primary metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), sustained QPS, cost-per-1k-queries ($), and token energy proxy (joules/token estimate from host telemetry).

Experiment details:
- Synthetic driver: 1000 simulated clients, Poisson arrivals, mean inter-arrival tuned to target sparse sessions (0.2 qps per client). Conversation length distribution: 70% 1-turn followups (6–40 tokens), 30% multi-turn (3–6 turns).
- Measurement window: 10-minute steady-state after 3-minute warm-up. Reported numbers are median of 3 runs.
- Cost model: infra CPU/GPU minute + inferred amortized kernel cost; represented as normalized $/1k queries for comparison rather than absolute invoice.

Representative numbers (annotated text chart):
Mode | slot | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | qps | $/1k
-----+------+---------+---------+---------+-----+-------
Opportunistic (no pacing) | n/a | 46 | 128 | 410 | 480 | 3.12
Slot 50ms | 50ms | 58 | 110 | 320 | 520 | 2.88
Slot 100ms | 100ms | 66 | 98 | 275 | 560 | 2.67
Slot 250ms | 250ms | 92 | 125 | 310 | 540 | 2.70
Notes: qps reflects successful completions/second; $/1k normalizes GPU amortized utilization. Results show a non-monotonic tradeoff: short slots (50ms) reduce tail relative to no pacing but increase p50; 100ms hits a sweet spot for this workload, increasing throughput and lowering $/1k. 250ms re-introduces higher p50 while throughput benefit diminishes (longer wait reduces cache reusability).

ASCII trend (p90 vs slot width):
slot-ms: 0    50    100   250
p90-ms: 128 - 110 - 98  - 125
(observed valley at ~100ms)

Observations and hypotheses:
- Small slot windows allow slightly larger batching without forcing long queuing; this increases kernel utilization and reduces unit cost.
- Too-large windows (>=250ms) accumulate queuing for short-turn sessions and increase median latency while hurting responsiveness; throughput bump flattens as arrivals no longer align with slot boundaries.
- Opportunistic multiplexing shows worst p99 (microbursts cause long tails). Pacing trades some median latency for a much reduced tail in mid-sized slot windows.
- KV-cache hit rates increased ~6% at 100ms vs opportunistic; suggests batching aligned with session prefixes improves reuse.

Telemetry snippets (examples):
- CPU steal events: opportunistic run had 1.8x more short-lived CPU steals correlated with p99 spikes.
- Kernel occupancy: mean occupancy at 100ms slot was 73%, opportunistic 58%.

Open questions / next runs:
1) Repeat on larger nodes (more vram) and with quantized kernels to see if sweet spot shifts.
2) Test hybrid policy: dynamic slot that shortens with high observed queue (adaptive 50–150ms).
3) Measure perceived latency in streaming scenarios (first-chunk latency vs final token). Pacing might worsen first-chunk latency even if tail improves.
4) Run end-to-end cost model that includes network egress, infra idle penalty, and console retention impact.

Action items:
- Priya: schedule 3-run matrix for {50,75,100,150,250}ms windows on large nodes (JIRA-OBS-1012). Due: 2028-05-24.
- Samir: add baseline with streaming-first-chunk instrumentation (GitHub PR linked).
- Maya: draft a small note for console heuristics proposing an "adaptive slot" option with default 100ms for assist-lite workloads.

Misc notes / scribbles:
- Observed a rare lock contention in runtime v2.7.2 when slot windows <25ms; deferring micro-optimizations until stability fix.
- Consider exposing slot metric in cost breakdown dashboard as "pacing delay" so customers can see tradeoffs.

Bottom line (working):
For short-turn, high-sparsity conversational workloads, a modest slot-pacing window (~100ms) can improve throughput and lower unit costs while trimming mid-tail latency. It is not a universal win — streaming-first-chunk latency and very short sessions can be harmed — so an adaptive runtime policy and clear console UX are required.

References:
- Related runs: github/pr/421 (bench harness), confluence/SlotPacing-Notes-2028, JIRA-OBS-987.
